# Core Four On Steroids — More, Better, New

**Source:** *$100M Leads*, "Core Four On Steroids: More Better New" (lines ~2714–2916).
This is how you scale the **Core Four** (Warm Outreach, Post Content, Cold Outreach, Paid Ads)
*on your own*, before you ever add Lead Getters. `hormozi-lead-more-better-new` runs this.

The premise: most owners plateau at $1M–$3M because they believe they've "saturated" their market —
**The Size Of The Pie Fallacy** (l.2878). They haven't. There are more leads out there than they can
imagine. There are exactly **two ways to boost *any* of the Core Four** to get more engaged leads on
your own, and they are easy to remember (l.2768–2770):

1. Do **More** of what you're currently doing.
2. Do what you're currently doing **Better**.
3. Do it somewhere **New**.

The three diagnostic questions to ask of your current advertising (l.2780):
> *Could you advertise more? Could you advertise better? Could you advertise somewhere new?*

**Run them in order — More first, then Better, then New (never jump to New to escape the work).** More
and Better work *with* each other more than separately; New is the last resort, only once More↔Better
returns run dry (l.2884, l.2896). The first question Hormozi asks before investing in a company that
needs customers: *"What's stopping them from doing ten times what they're currently doing?"* (l.2904).

---

## 1 — MORE (do this first)

You already know your advertising works to *some* degree. The next obvious move is **more — a lot
more**. Crank volume to your max capacity. Even with **no improvements at all, if you double your
inputs you get more engaged leads** (l.2786): twice the reach outs, twice the content, twice the ads,
double the ad spend. The biggest increases often come from More, not Better (l.2790).

### The Rule of 100 — the engine of More (l.2792–2794)

> Do **100 primary actions every day, for 100 days in a row.** That's it.

This is the one promise in the book: 100 primary actions/day for 100 straight days *will* get you more
engaged leads. Applied to each Core Four activity (l.2796–2826):

| Core Four activity | Daily Rule-of-100 target | Example primary actions |
|---|---|---|
| **Warm Reach Outs** | 100 reach outs per day | email, text, direct message, calls |
| **Post Content** | 100 **minutes** per day making content; release ≥1 per day on a platform (post more as you improve) | short & long videos or articles, podcasts, infographics |
| **Cold Reach Outs** | 100 reach outs per day *(expect lower response rates — use automation)* | email, text, direct message, cold call, flyers |
| **Paid Ads** | 100 **minutes** per day making paid ads; run them 100 days straight | direct-response media ads, direct mail, seminar, podcast spots |

- Content and Paid Ads are measured in **100 minutes of production**, not 100 posts — outreach is
  measured in **100 outreaches**. Keep the distinction exact.
- For Paid Ads, use the **daily budget** from the paid-ads chapter and aim for **Client-Financed
  Acquisition** (l.2826).

---

## 2 — BETTER (do this in parallel, once More "breaks")

Getting better gets you **more leads for the same effort**. You get better by exactly one activity:
**testing**. You do More and More until it *breaks* — your CAC eventually climbs too high to sustain —
and that's the signal to make it Better (l.2832). "Thousands of these tiny tests separate the winners
from the beginners."

### Test at the constraint (l.2834)

Every action a lead takes before becoming a customer is a potential **drop-off point**. Do the most
testing at whatever step the **most leads drop off** — Hormozi calls these **constraints**: the points
where the smallest improvement creates the biggest boost. Worked example (l.2836–2848):

```
30% Optin
 5% Apply     ← the constraint (biggest drop-off)
50% Schedule
```

Improving *each* step by 5 percentage points yields wildly different results — which is why you attack
the constraint:

- 30% → 35% Optin = **16%** more leads (1.16x)
- 5% → 10% Apply = **100%** more leads (2x)  ← the constraint wins by far
- 50% → 55% Schedule = **10%** more leads (1.1x)

Rule: **focus on the constraint**; if unsure which step it is, find where the most leads drop off.

### Test one thing per week per platform (l.2852–2862)

Four reasons for one test at a time, per platform:

1. Test multiple things at once and you never learn what actually worked.
2. **Steps affect each other** — one change can move results at another step (more opt-ins but fewer
   applies = no bueno). One change lets you *see* what happened.
3. It forces you to **prioritize** — tests are infinite, time isn't. Don't waste a test on "red to
   bright red."
4. You run it **long enough** to see a real improvement. Too short = not enough data; too long = wasted
   time. One week is typically long enough.

### The weekly testing cadence (l.2864–2870)

- **Every Monday:** run one split test per platform. Give it a week.
- **The next Monday, do three things:**
  1. Look at the results and pick the **winner** for each platform test.
  2. **Write the result into a log of all tests** — so next time you start "a zillion improvements
     later, not at square one."
  3. Design the next test to beat your current *best* version.
- **Stopping rule:** if you can't beat the current version in **four tries (or one month)**, move on to
  the next constraint (l.2870).

Better has diminishing returns. When the effort you put into Better brings lower returns than that same
effort spent elsewhere — *only then* do you go New (l.2872).

---

## 3 — NEW (last, and hardest)

Once More and Better are exhausted, the only lever left is **new places, in new ways** (l.2876).

**When to go New (l.2884):** when the returns from More↔Better are **lower than what you'd get from a
new placement or new way of advertising.** New is harder in practice, which is exactly why you exhaust
More↔Better first (l.2896).

### The three kinds of New, in priority order (l.2886–2892)

The order comes down to one rule — **what gets the most leads for the amount of work.** Nine times out
of ten:

> **New Placements → New Platforms → New Core Four activity**

1. **New placements** — same platform, other places/forms of content (Instagram stories, messenger
   ads, posts; YouTube shorts, longs, community posts).
2. **New platforms** — carry a placement you know to a new platform (IG messenger → FB messenger;
   YouTube shorts → Instagram reels). *Then*, once you know the platform, add new placements on it.
3. **New Core Four activity** — add an entirely new Core Four activity on top of what you already run.

---

## The loop (summary — l.2902–2906)

1. Do **way more** of what works until it "breaks."
2. The **next drop-off point** becomes obvious → keep the volume up while you go back and fix that
   **constraint** (Better). More and Better run together.
3. Only once More↔Better is exhausted, go **New**: new placements on a platform you know → known
   placements on a new platform → new placements on that new platform → a new Core Four activity.
4. Each time you add a New, measure it, then **scale it back up with More↔Better. Rinse and repeat.**

**Sequencing note (l.2914–2916):** after warm outreach seeds your first customers — if you have *more
time than money*, add posting content; if *more money than time*, add cold outreach or paid ads. You
only need **one** Core Four activity to start. Pick one, then max it out: **More → Better → New.**

---

## Output contract for `hormozi-lead-more-better-new`

Given the user's current advertising, produce:
1. **Diagnosis** — which Core Four they run today, at what volume, and the answer to "what stops you
   from doing 10x?"
2. **More plan** — the Rule-of-100 daily target for their activity (100 actions or 100 minutes), and
   the specific volume increase.
3. **Better plan** — their funnel steps with the **constraint** named (biggest drop-off), the one
   weekly test to run against it, and the Monday/Monday cadence + test log.
4. **New plan** — the next placement → platform → Core Four move, in priority order, with the
   "most leads per unit work" rationale.
5. Numbers pulled from the product's real funnel or marked `<placeholder>` — never fabricated.

## Sources and basis

*$100M Leads* — "How To Get Even More Leads: More Better New" framing (l.2764–2782); More + Rule of 100
applied to the Core Four (l.2784–2828); Better — constraints, one-test-per-week, weekly cadence,
four-tries stopping rule (l.2830–2872); New — Size Of The Pie Fallacy, when-to, placements→platforms→
core-four order (l.2874–2900); summary + sequencing (l.2902–2916). Cross-reference:
`rule-of-100-and-roadmap.md` for the full Rule of 100 / Open To Goal treatment.
